validation.note: Bugfix roadmap per nw-bugfix minimal flow. RCA was established empirically (baseline container repro, fix-candidate run, chart-shaped control) rather than by a five-whys pass, and approved by the maintainer 2026-09-20.

phases.name: One address mechanism per startup surface
phases.description: Stop declaring listening addresses twice, so Kestrel no longer reports a discarded address source as a startup Warning that the Task Manager shows to users as a problem.

steps.name: Regression guard for colliding address declarations
criteria: A failing NUnit test asserts the Dockerfile does not leave an inherited address variable in force while it defines Kestrel:Endpoints.
The same test asserts no launch profile sets applicationUrl while appsettings.Development.json defines Kestrel:Endpoints.
The test asserts the Helm ConfigMap declares no address variable alongside its Kestrel endpoint keys.
The test fails against current code on the Dockerfile and launch profile counts, proving both collisions exist.
The test names the offending surface and variable in its failure message, so a future breakage is actionable without reading the test.
steps.implementation_notes: Follows the repository-file guard idiom already used by UsageDataDisclosureTest and ExpandOnlyMigrationGuardTest: anchor on Lighthouse.sln, take its parent as the repository root, read the shipped file and assert on its text. The guarded surfaces are a closed list. render.yaml is deliberately absent from it and the reason is stated in the test, because it still declares ASPNETCORE_URLS and would red the suite over a deployment whose status is unresolved.

steps.name: Single address mechanism on both surfaces
criteria: The Dockerfile clears the address variable the base image sets, beside the Kestrel endpoint keys it already defines.
The http and https launch profiles no longer set applicationUrl.
The backend suite stays green with the live-connector categories excluded.
A container run of an image built from the changed Dockerfile logs no override warning and binds the same ports as before.
steps.implementation_notes: Kestrel:Endpoints stays as the single mechanism because the Dockerfile, the Helm chart and the CI workflows already use it; moving the other way would mean changing all three. The Helm chart needs no edit of its own, because the pod inherits the cleared variable from the image. The dev ports are unchanged: appsettings.Development.json already defines both endpoints, so dropping applicationUrl removes the duplicate rather than the port.
